summary: 1. Write titles and first lines in Devanagari Hindi script; native script videos average 60%+ stayed rates while English/Romanized titles drop below 38%. 2. Begin immediately with vivid, physical visual metaphors (e.g., '3 cars stacked on your teeth') rather than dry academic questions. 3. Frame hooks around immediate viewer perspective using direct triggers like 'सोचो...' (Imagine...) or bold paradoxical statements. 4. Keep content tightly trimmed under 25 seconds; longer videos (40s+) suffer severe drop-offs and low stayed percentages. 5. Focus topics on pop-culture physics comparisons (T. Rex vs Cars, Crash dynamics) instead of obscure chemistry or engineering facts.
winning_hooks: Direct viewer imagination triggers using 'सोचो...' (Imagine...) paired with everyday object comparisons
Immediate counter-intuitive facts stated as baseline truths (e.g., 'जो car crash में पिचक जाती है, वो तुम्हें ज़्यादा बचाती है')
avoid: English and Romanized Hinglish script in titles and hooks
Academic and multi-clause question hooks like 'वैज्ञानिकों को ऐसी सूक्ष्म आकृतियां क्यों मिली हैं...'
Videos with durations over 40 seconds before fixing initial retention
next_experiment: A/B test a 20-second Devanagari video: Version A starts with a 'सोचो...' imagination hook vs Version B starting with a 3-second paradoxical fact hook on the exact same T. Rex topic.
